title: Judges Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 1.

questions.question: Who did the children of Israel ask to determine who should fight the Canaanites first?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:1 states that the children of Israel asked the LORD who should go up against the Canaanites first.

questions.question: Which tribe did the LORD say should go up first against the Canaanites?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:2 records that the LORD said Judah shall go up first against the Canaanites.

questions.question: Who did Judah invite to join him in fighting against the Canaanites?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:3 shows Judah inviting his brother Simeon to come up with him to fight against the Canaanites.

questions.question: How many men did Judah and Simeon reportedly kill in Bezek?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:4 states that they slew ten thousand men in Bezek.

questions.question: What happened to Adonibezek after he was caught?
options: His thumbs and great toes were cut off
questions.correctAnswer: His thumbs and great toes were cut off
questions.explanation: Judges 1:6 explains that Adonibezek had his thumbs and great toes cut off after being caught.

questions.question: True or False: Adonibezek said God had requited him as he had done to others.
questions.explanation: In Judges 1:7, Adonibezek acknowledges that God repaid him as he had done to seventy kings.

questions.question: What city did the children of Judah take and set on fire?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:8 states that Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, and set the city on fire.

questions.question: True or False: After Jerusalem, Judah fought the Canaanites only in the valley.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:9 explains Judah fought the Canaanites in the mountain, in the south, and in the valley, not only in the valley.

questions.question: Which three men were slain by Judah in Hebron?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:10 notes that Judah slew Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai in Hebron.

questions.question: What was Debir formerly called?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:11 tells us Debir was formerly called Kirjathsepher.

questions.question: Who promised his daughter Achsah in marriage to the one who captured Kirjathsepher?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:12 states Caleb promised Achsah to whoever captured Kirjathsepher.

questions.question: True or False: Othniel, Caleb's younger brother, took Kirjathsepher and married Achsah.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:13 confirms that Othniel took Kirjathsepher and married Achsah.

questions.question: What did Achsah ask her father Caleb for after marriage?
options: A blessing and springs of water
questions.correctAnswer: A blessing and springs of water
questions.explanation: Judges 1:15 shows Achsah asking Caleb for a blessing and also for springs of water.

questions.question: In what order did these events occur: (1) Judah asks Simeon to join him, (2) Judah fights Jerusalem, (3) The LORD says Judah will go up first?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:2 shows the LORD saying Judah will go up first, then Judges 1:3 Judah invites Simeon, followed by Judges 1:8 where Judah fights Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: After Joshua's death, the children of Israel immediately drove out all the Canaanites from the land.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:28 indicates that although Israel was strong, they put the Canaanites to tribute and did not utterly drive them out.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How does Caleb's giving of his daughter Achsah to Othniel illustrate a biblical principle of faith and reward?
options: It shows that faithfulness in battle leads to blessings
It demonstrates the importance of wealth in marriage
It teaches that marriage should be arranged by parents alone
It emphasizes the need for political alliances
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that faithfulness in battle leads to blessings
questions.explanation: Caleb promised Achsah to whoever captured Kirjathsepher (Judges 1:12), and Othniel took it and received her as wife (Judges 1:13). This shows that faith and courage in fulfilling God's commands are rewarded, emphasizing faithfulness in action (Judges 1:12-13).

questions.question: What did Achsah request from her father Caleb after marriage, and what does this teach about practical faith?
options: A blessing and springs of water, showing trust in God's provision
A royal title for her husband
questions.correctAnswer: A blessing and springs of water, showing trust in God's provision
questions.explanation: Achsah asked Caleb for a blessing and specifically requested springs of water (Judges 1:15), showing her practical faith in God's provision for daily needs. Caleb granted her request (Judges 1:15), highlighting trust and reliance on God's blessings.

questions.question: How does the cooperation between Judah and Simeon in destroying Zephath (Hormah) illustrate biblical unity?
options: It shows the strength in brotherly cooperation for God's purposes
It reveals that Simeon was the senior leader
It suggests that only Judah could defeat the Canaanites
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the strength in brotherly cooperation for God's purposes
questions.explanation: Judah asked Simeon to join in fighting (Judges 1:3) and together they destroyed Zephath, renaming it Hormah (Judges 1:17). This demonstrates unity and cooperation among God's people to accomplish His will.

questions.question: According to Judges 1:19, why could Judah not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, and what does this teach about trusting God in difficulties?
options: Because the inhabitants had chariots of iron, showing the challenge of trusting God amid strong opposition
Because the people were too numerous
questions.correctAnswer: Because the inhabitants had chariots of iron, showing the challenge of trusting God amid strong opposition
questions.explanation: Judah was unable to drive out valley inhabitants due to their iron chariots (Judges 1:19). Despite the LORD's presence, obstacles remain, teaching believers to depend continually on God even when challenges seem overwhelming.

questions.question: What does the story of the man from Bethel who showed the spies the entrance tell us about mercy and integrity?
options: Showing mercy to the man and his family honored his integrity and led to mercy being promised
The spies ignored the man after receiving help
The man was punished for aiding the spies
The city was spared because of the man's actions
questions.correctAnswer: Showing mercy to the man and his family honored his integrity and led to mercy being promised
questions.explanation: The spies promised mercy to the man if he showed them the city entrance (Judges 1:24). After he complied, they spared him and his family (Judges 1:25), illustrating the value of integrity and the importance of mercy in God's people.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Benjamin completely drove out the Jebusites from Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:21 states that Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites, who continued to dwell in Jerusalem with them. This reminds believers that incomplete obedience can lead to ongoing challenges.

questions.question: How does Judges 1:20 teach about faithfulness to promises and God's faithfulness?
options: Caleb received Hebron as Moses promised, showing God's faithfulness to keep His word
Caleb lost Hebron because of disobedience
Hebron was taken by another tribe
The promise was conditional on military strength
questions.correctAnswer: Caleb received Hebron as Moses promised, showing God's faithfulness to keep His word
questions.explanation: The verse states Hebron was given to Caleb as Moses had promised (Judges 1:20), illustrating that God's promises are fulfilled when His people are faithful.

questions.question: What lesson about prayer and seeking God's guidance can be learned from Israel asking the LORD who should fight first after Joshua's death?
options: Seeking God's direction is essential before taking action
Leaders should decide without asking God
Immediate action without consultation is best
The people chose their own leader
questions.correctAnswer: Seeking God's direction is essential before taking action
questions.explanation: Judges 1:1 shows Israel asking the LORD who should lead the fight, and the LORD directing Judah (Judges 1:2). This underscores the importance of prayer and seeking God's guidance in decisions.

questions.question: True or False: The house of Joseph was successful in capturing Bethel because the LORD was with them.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:22 confirms that the house of Joseph went up against Bethel and that the LORD was with them. This teaches believers that God’s presence is crucial for success.

questions.question: What does the movement of the Kenites with the children of Judah into the wilderness teach about fellowship and support among God’s people?
options: It shows the importance of unity and dwelling together for mutual support
It indicates the Kenites were forced to leave
It suggests the Kenites were enemies of Judah
It points to isolation as a spiritual principle
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the importance of unity and dwelling together for mutual support
questions.explanation: Judges 1:16 states the Kenites moved with Judah into the wilderness and dwelt among the people, illustrating the biblical principle of fellowship and mutual support.

questions.question: How does the example of Caleb giving Achsah the upper and nether springs after her request illustrate generosity?
options: Caleb generously granted her request, showing willingness to bless others
Caleb refused her request to keep the land
Achsah took the springs by force
The springs were given only after a dispute
questions.correctAnswer: Caleb generously granted her request, showing willingness to bless others
questions.explanation: Achsah asked for springs of water (Judges 1:15), and Caleb gave her both upper and nether springs, demonstrating generosity and blessing others as a model for Christian living.

questions.question: Which city was renamed Hormah after Judah and Simeon utterly destroyed it?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:17 states that Judah and Simeon destroyed Zephath and then called it Hormah, showing the significance of obedience leading to victory and new beginnings.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 1 teaches that incomplete obedience in driving out Canaanites led to their continued presence among Israel.
questions.explanation: Verses such as Judges 1:27-33 describe how tribes did not drive out the Canaanites fully, resulting in them dwelling among Israel, illustrating the consequence of partial obedience.

questions.question: What does the story of the man from Bethel building another city called Luz teach about integrity and new beginnings?
options: Even after losing his city, the man started anew, showing resilience and integrity
He betrayed Israel and was punished
He was forgotten by the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: Even after losing his city, the man started anew, showing resilience and integrity
questions.explanation: Judges 1:26 says the man went to the land of the Hittites and built a new city called Luz. This shows that integrity and faithfulness can lead to new beginnings despite setbacks.

questions.question: What does Judges 1:18 reveal about Judah’s military achievements and God’s blessing?
options: Judah took Gaza, Askelon, and Ekron with their coasts, showing God’s blessing on their efforts
Judah failed to capture any cities
Judah made peace with the Canaanites instead
Judah lost many battles in the south
questions.correctAnswer: Judah took Gaza, Askelon, and Ekron with their coasts, showing God’s blessing on their efforts
questions.explanation: Judges 1:18 states Judah took these cities, highlighting God's favor on their obedience and faith in battle.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 1.

questions.question: Which city did the man who showed the spies the entrance to the city go on to build in the land of the Hittites?
questions.explanation: According to Judges 1:26, the man went into the land of the Hittites and built a city, calling it Luz, the same name as the original city.

questions.question: Which tribe did not drive out the inhabitants of Bethshean and its towns, allowing the Canaanites to dwell there?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:27 states that Manasseh did not drive out the inhabitants of Bethshean and her towns, and the Canaanites continued to live there.

questions.question: What happened when Israel became strong according to Judges 1:28?
options: They completely drove out the Canaanites
They put the Canaanites to tribute but did not completely drive them out
They were defeated by the Canaanites
questions.correctAnswer: They put the Canaanites to tribute but did not completely drive them out
questions.explanation: Judges 1:28 explains that Israel, though strong, did not utterly drive out the Canaanites but subjected them to tribute.

questions.question: Which tribe did not drive out the Canaanites dwelling in Gezer?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:29 clearly states that Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, allowing them to dwell among them.

questions.question: What was the fate of the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol according to Judges 1:30?
options: They became tributaries after dwelling among Zebulun
questions.correctAnswer: They became tributaries after dwelling among Zebulun
questions.explanation: Judges 1:30 states that Zebulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol; the Canaanites dwelt among them and became tributaries.

questions.question: Which tribe dwelt among the Canaanites instead of driving them out, as described in Judges 1:32?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:32 says the Asherites dwelt among the Canaanites because they did not drive them out.

questions.question: What was the relationship between Naphtali and the inhabitants of Bethshemesh and Bethanath according to Judges 1:33?
options: Naphtali dwelt among them but the inhabitants became tributaries
Naphtali made war and destroyed the towns
Naphtali formed an alliance with them
questions.correctAnswer: Naphtali dwelt among them but the inhabitants became tributaries
questions.explanation: Judges 1:33 reveals that Naphtali did not drive out the inhabitants but dwelt among them, and the inhabitants became tributaries.

questions.question: What effect did the Amorites have on the children of Dan as described in Judges 1:34?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:34 states that the Amorites forced the children of Dan into the mountains, not allowing them to come down to the valley.

questions.question: Did the Amorites continue to live in Mount Heres in Aijalon and Shaalbim despite Joseph's hand prevailing?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:35 confirms that although the Amorites dwelt in Mount Heres in Aijalon and Shaalbim, the house of Joseph prevailed so that the Amorites became tributaries.

questions.question: Which of the following cities did Manasseh fail to drive out the inhabitants from, according to Judges 1:27?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:27 lists Megiddo among the towns where Manasseh did not drive out the inhabitants, allowing Canaanites to dwell there.

questions.question: The name 'Luz' appears in Judges 1:23-26. What literary device is illustrated by the man building a new city named Luz after fleeing the original city?
questions.explanation: The repetition of the name 'Luz' in the original city and the new city built by the man forms an inclusio, framing the narrative and emphasizing continuity (Judges 1:23-26).

questions.question: Which Hebrew word meaning is significant for understanding the term 'tributaries' used in this chapter regarding Canaanites' relationships?
options: Masach (to wipe out or blot out)
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root 'Masar' implies delivering or giving over, which relates to the Canaanites being subjected or 'tributaries' to Israel as mentioned in Judges 1:28, 30, and 33.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of incomplete conquest and coexistence with Canaanites seen in Judges 1?
questions.explanation: Joshua 13:1-7 discusses lands not yet conquered and the presence of Canaanite inhabitants, paralleling Judges 1's themes of incomplete driving out and coexistence.

questions.question: How does Judges 1:19 relate to the broader biblical theme of divine assistance and human limitation?
options: It shows complete human conquest without God
It highlights Israel's failure despite God's presence
It demonstrates God's presence with Judah yet human limits due to iron chariots
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God's presence with Judah yet human limits due to iron chariots
questions.explanation: Judges 1:19 states that although the LORD was with Judah, they could not drive out the valley inhabitants because of their iron chariots, showing divine aid paired with human limitations.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of partial obedience and incomplete conquest seen in Judges 1?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 3:7-19 warns against unbelief that prevents entering God's rest, echoing Israel's incomplete conquest and disobedience from Judges 1.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by Judah's dependence on God's guidance to lead the attack against the Canaanites?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:2 shows God directing Judah to lead the fight, demonstrating Divine Providence where God sovereignly guides His people’s actions.

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized by the LORD delivering the Canaanites and Perizzites into Judah's hand?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:4 reveals God's omnipotence as He empowers Judah to overcome powerful enemies by delivering them into their hands.

questions.question: What theological insight can be drawn from Adonibezek’s statement about the seventy kings with their thumbs and toes cut off?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:7 shows Adonibezek acknowledging God’s justice in requiting him as he had done to others, illustrating divine retribution (lex talionis).

questions.question: How does the capture and burning of Jerusalem by Judah contribute to the redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: It foreshadows the future purification and conquest of Jerusalem by God's people.
It demonstrates the permanent destruction of all Canaanite peoples.
It signifies the end of all God's promises to Israel.
It illustrates the rejection of God's covenant.
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the future purification and conquest of Jerusalem by God's people.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:8 connects to the broader biblical theme of God’s people gradually taking possession of the Promised Land, a foreshadowing of ultimate redemption and restoration (cf. Joshua 6).

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by Caleb’s promise to give his daughter Achsah in marriage to the one who captures Kirjathsepher?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:12 reveals covenantal blessings—Caleb’s promise demonstrates God’s provision and reward to those who obey and conquer, reflecting covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What combined theological teaching about God’s provision and human responsibility is seen in Judges 1:12 and Judges 1:13?
options: God rewards obedience through covenant promises and human action is necessary to receive blessings.
God’s blessings are automatic and require no human effort.
Human effort alone secures blessings without divine involvement.
Blessings are purely spiritual and unrelated to earthly actions.
questions.correctAnswer: God rewards obedience through covenant promises and human action is necessary to receive blessings.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:12 shows Caleb’s promise contingent on human action, and 1:13 shows Othniel’s obedience resulting in receiving Achsah, illustrating the synergy of divine provision and human responsibility.

questions.question: What attribute of God is reflected when He grants Caleb springs of water upon Achsah's request?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:15 shows Caleb generously giving both upper and lower springs, reflecting God's generous blessings upon His people through human agents.

questions.question: What does the presence of the Kenites, Moses’ father-in-law’s family, dwelling with Judah reveal about God’s providence and covenant faithfulness?
options: God’s providence extends protection to covenant allies and their descendants.
God allows all peoples equal status regardless of covenant.
God’s covenant is exclusively ethnic with no room for alliance.
God’s providence is arbitrary and unpredictable.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence extends protection to covenant allies and their descendants.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:16 shows the Kenites joining Judah, indicating God's providential care for covenant-related families, continuing His faithfulness beyond Israel’s descent.

questions.question: How do Judges 1:19 and 1:28 together inform our understanding of the doctrine of sanctification in the conquest of Canaan?
options: Sanctification is a progressive struggle where God enables victory but does not complete full cleansing immediately.
Sanctification is instantaneous and complete without any remaining sin or evil.
Sanctification is irrelevant to the conquest narrative.
Sanctification requires human effort alone without divine aid.
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification is a progressive struggle where God enables victory but does not complete full cleansing immediately.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:19 shows God aiding Judah but not fully driving out enemies, and 1:28 shows incomplete expulsion of Canaanites, illustrating sanctification as an ongoing process rather than instant perfection.

questions.question: What apologetic response does Judges 1:21 give to sceptics claiming the Israelites were unjust conquerors because they failed to fully drive out the Jebusites?
options: The Israelites did not fully conquer some peoples, showing God’s allowance of coexistence and judgment over time.
The Israelites were completely unjust and disobedient, making their conquest illegitimate.
The Israelites exterminated all peoples without exception.
The conquest was a myth with no historical basis.
questions.correctAnswer: The Israelites did not fully conquer some peoples, showing God’s allowance of coexistence and judgment over time.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:21 states the Jebusites remained with Benjamin, indicating God’s sovereign timing in judgment and conquest, countering sceptics who claim Israel's conquest was entirely ruthless or complete.

questions.question: What doctrinal lesson can be drawn from the house of Joseph's use of a spy to capture Bethel as narrated in Judges 1:22-25?
options: God’s people may use wisdom and human strategy under divine guidance to accomplish His purposes.
God’s people rely solely on miraculous intervention without human involvement.
God does not permit espionage or strategy among His people.
Military conquest is always by force alone without intelligence efforts.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s people may use wisdom and human strategy under divine guidance to accomplish His purposes.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:22-25 shows Joseph’s house preparing by sending spies, with God's presence, illustrating that God’s providence includes human wisdom and strategy.

questions.question: How does the narrative of the man escaping from Bethel to the land of the Hittites and building a city called Luz (Judges 1:25-26) contribute to the biblical theme of human sin and divine judgment?
options: It shows human attempts to evade divine judgment can lead to spreading sin elsewhere.
It illustrates immediate repentance and restoration.
It demonstrates the futility of human rebellion with no consequences.
It signifies divine acceptance of all human actions.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows human attempts to evade divine judgment can lead to spreading sin elsewhere.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:25-26 narrates the escape and city building by a man from Bethel, symbolizing that sin and rebellion persist beyond initial judgment, echoing humanity’s ongoing fallenness.

questions.question: What combined theological principle about partial obedience and its consequences is derived from Judges 1:27 and Judges 1:29-33?
options: Partial obedience leads to coexistence with sin and becoming tributaries, showing the danger of incomplete sanctification.
Partial obedience is as good as full obedience in God’s eyes.
Partial obedience results in complete blessing and victory.
God ignores partial obedience and only rewards total failure.
questions.correctAnswer: Partial obedience leads to coexistence with sin and becoming tributaries, showing the danger of incomplete sanctification.
questions.explanation: Verses 27 and 29-33 describe Israel’s failure to fully drive out Canaanites, resulting in coexistence and tribute, illustrating the biblical principle that incomplete obedience leads to spiritual compromise.

questions.question: What redemptive theological insight arises from the Amorites forcing the children of Dan into the mountains (Judges 1:34) while the house of Joseph prevails over them (Judges 1:35)?
options: God’s deliverance is selective, demonstrating His sovereign will and the ongoing struggle between obedience and opposition.
God uniformly blesses all tribes without distinction.
God abandons those who fail to obey.
God’s victory is automatic and universal without resistance.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s deliverance is selective, demonstrating His sovereign will and the ongoing struggle between obedience and opposition.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:34-35 shows varied outcomes for tribes, reflecting the complex reality of God’s sovereign will in partial deliverance and ongoing spiritual warfare in the conquest.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching about God’s justice and retribution is conveyed by the cutting off of thumbs and great toes of Adonibezek and the seventy kings (Judges 1:6-7)?
options: God enacts just retribution corresponding to one’s deeds, affirming His righteous judgment.
God overlooks human sin and does not judge.
God’s justice is arbitrary and unpredictable.
God’s justice is limited to spiritual matters only.
questions.correctAnswer: God enacts just retribution corresponding to one’s deeds, affirming His righteous judgment.
questions.explanation: Judges 1:6-7 depict Adonibezek’s punishment as a direct recompense for his own actions, illustrating the doctrine of divine justice and retributive punishment.
